summary: The change adds hir/abap indent/Format implementing the abaplint two-space style, routes every generator (hir, llvm, ts, tsfront drivers, wasm single/multi-class/interface) through Format, and the golden file diff is whitespace-only; go build and go test ./... pass and all listed acceptance cases (classes, sections, CASE/WHEN, TRY/CATCH/CLEANUP, report events, GET RUN TIME, same-line statements, literals/comments, 255-byte wrapping) behave as specified. Remaining issues are edge cases: wrapping can cut right before a `*` token so the continuation becomes a column-0 comment on re-format (idempotency/semantics), a long trailing " comment makes Format error instead of wrapping, and some non-block statements (GET TIME STAMP, INTERFACE ... DEFERRED, CLASS ... LOCAL FRIENDS, SELECT without ENDSELECT) are misclassified as block openers/events.

findings.claim: lastSafeSpace may cut immediately before a `*` token, so the wrapped continuation line starts with `*`. On the next Format pass indentABAP treats that line as a full-line comment and moves it to column 0, so Format is not idempotent and the statement's tail silently turns into a comment; at report level (indent 0) even the first pass emits `* zz + 1.` at column 0, which ABAP itself reads as a comment.
findings.repro:
Format("CLASS c IMPLEMENTATION.
METHOD m.
IF a = 1.
x = " + strings.Repeat("a",243) + " * zz + bbb.
ENDIF.
ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
") then Format again: second output has `* zz + bbb.` at column 0 and ENDIF mis-indented. Also Format("REPORT z.
x = "+strings.Repeat("a",250)+" * zz + 1.
WRITE x.
") yields a column-0 `* zz + 1.` line.

findings.claim: A statement with a long trailing " comment cannot be wrapped: lastSafeSpace stops at the comment start, the remainder line begins with `"`, and the loop returns 'unbreakable source line' instead of wrapping the comment text (wrapComment already exists for that). llvm and wasm emit trailing comments (e.g. `" offset to field %s`), so a long one aborts code generation (panic in llvm.Compile / wasm.CompileInterface).
findings.repro:
Format("METHOD m.
x = 1. "" + strings.Repeat("word ", 70) + "
ENDMETHOD.
") returns err 'unbreakable source line (353 bytes)'.

findings.claim: isReportEvent treats every GET except RUN/PARAMETER/REFERENCE as a report event, so runtime statements like `GET TIME STAMP FIELD ts.`, `GET TIME.`, `GET BIT`, `GET BADI`, `GET CURSOR`, `GET PF-STATUS` are put at column 0 and open an event block, mis-indenting the surrounding FORM/METHOD body.
findings.repro:
Format("FORM f.
GET TIME STAMP FIELD ts.
WRITE ts.
ENDFORM.
") gives `GET TIME STAMP FIELD ts.` at column 0 instead of two spaces.

findings.claim: `INTERFACE x DEFERRED.` unconditionally opens an INTERFACE block, and `CLASS x DEFINITION LOCAL FRIENDS ...` / `CLASS x DEFINITION LOAD.` open a CLASS block (only ' DEFERRED' is excluded). Everything after such a forward declaration is indented one extra level until an unmatched END statement appears.
findings.repro:
Format("INTERFACE zif DEFERRED.
CLASS zcl DEFINITION.
PUBLIC SECTION.
INTERFACES zif.
ENDCLASS.
") indents CLASS/ENDCLASS by two spaces; same with "CLASS zcl DEFINITION LOCAL FRIENDS ltcl.
CLASS ltcl DEFINITION.
ENDCLASS.
".

findings.claim: A forward declaration (CLASS ... DEFINITION DEFERRED) inside a report event body is forced to column 0 and pops the event, so following event statements lose their indentation; abaplint keeps a deferred declaration as an ordinary statement inside the event.
findings.repro:
Format("START-OF-SELECTION.
CLASS lcl DEFINITION DEFERRED.
WRITE 'x'.
") emits both lines at column 0.

findings.claim: SELECT is treated as a block opener unless it contains ' SINGLE ' or ' INTO TABLE '; aggregate selects (SELECT COUNT(*) ... INTO @DATA(n).), APPENDING TABLE, INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF TABLE etc. have no ENDSELECT and leave a dangling block that indents the rest of the routine.
findings.repro:
Format("FORM f.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t INTO @DATA(n).
WRITE n.
ENDFORM.
") indents WRITE by four spaces.

findings.claim: CompileMultiClass formats MainClass, ChunkClasses, Interfaces and StateClass, then r.Files() formats each of them again; and the chunk cost estimate still uses the old wrapLongLines (240-byte wrap, no re-indent) while the final output is produced by Format (255-byte wrap plus indentation), so line budgets are computed against a different layout than what is emitted.

formatABAP (and wasm.CompileInterface) panic on a Format error instead of propagating it; before this change llvm.Compile never failed, so an unbreakable line now crashes the tool rather than returning an error like the other call sites.
